**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Tuley opens by stating his own method rather than a projection: longtime readers of his columns know he would rather be a year early on a team peaking than a year late, and he is not deterred by a bet coming up short. He bet Texas to win the playoff last season and lost it when Arch Manning did not reach his potential as quickly as hoped; he read the Longhorns' disappointing year as showing signs of competence and is betting that he was simply early, drawing an explicit parallel to backing the Detroit Lions again after losing with them. He notes Texas is the second betting choice in the SEC behind Georgia.

*Rests on:* quarterback (Arch Manning's development); the contributor's stated willingness to be early

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Tuley notes he was not a believer in Indiana for most of last season but took the Hoosiers at +330 to win the playoff in the VSiN Bowl Betting Guide and rode them to the title. He acknowledges the loss of Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza as the NFL's No. 1 overall pick, but credits Curt Cignetti with one of the biggest turnarounds in the sport's history and says he is confident Indiana will be in the running again. He reads the Big Ten as a three-horse race between Indiana, Ohio State and Oregon, which makes +245 a fair price, and adds he might also take a shot at the Hoosiers repeating as national champion.

*Rests on:* coaching (Cignetti); replacing a departed Heisman-winning quarterback; the contributor's read that the league is a three-way race
